title: Etale descent from a flat Noetherian base change near a local closed point
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative local ring and $T$ a Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $t:T\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $g:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ be any scheme morphism. Suppose $a:E\to Y$ and $p:E\to T$ form a cartesian square with $g,t$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $V\subset T$ be open such that $p|_V$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. If $v\in V$ maps to the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$, then $g$ is etale. No finiteness of $g$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0EYA final descent detail; Tag 02VN, etale is fpqc local on the base

proof.text:
The composite V -> T -> Spec B is flat. For any point b of Spec B,
b specializes to the closed point. Generalizing maps lift this specialization
through the supplied point v in V, giving a point of V mapping to b. Thus
V -> Spec B is surjective. Since T is Noetherian, every open is quasi-compact
and every map from V is quasi-compact. Restrict the supplied cartesian square
to V, and apply fpqc descent of etaleness. The implementation first restricts
the base and Y to their top opens; compose with the top-open isomorphisms to
recover the original g. No finiteness assumption on g is needed. Empty Y and
V = T are included; hv ensures V is nonempty.
